description: Field-service and hardware-maintenance firms (ATM cash-handling, safes, CIT, terminal repair) in ME beyond Payten are essentially invisible in web search.
No ME public-procurement channel was mined this run, yet state banks/institutions publish tenders naming winning IT vendors and contract values.
Montenegrin Cyrillic-script and ijekavian spelling variants were only lightly exercised.
Vendor employment and project signals (job ads, LinkedIn project posts, conference sponsor lists) were not systematically harvested, though they often name bank projects before marketing pages do.
Vendor reference pages are undated, so wins cannot be time-ordered from the page alone.
Vendor partner-locator and 'find a partner' tools were not interrogated directly — they are typically JavaScript applications that web search cannot index.
Card-personalisation and identity vendors (Thales, IDEMIA, Giesecke+Devrient, Veridos) and cash-handling vendors (Glory, CIMA) were not searched against Montenegro in this pass.

Vendor-side evidence hidden in bank parent-group IT disclosures (NLB, OTP/CKB, Erste, Addiko, Ziraat, Adriatic Bank owners) was not covered — group-level vendor contracts often determine the ME subsidiary's stack.

Vendor conference and roadshow material (Asseco/Payten SEE user conferences, Mastercard/Visa regional events, Sibos/Money Motion/Fintech Adria agendas) frequently names ME bank clients in speaker bios and session titles, and was not searched.
This pass surfaced ME vendor references from 2015 (ASEE/Ziraat) and 2022 (Payten/Hipotekarna) but almost nothing from 2023-2026, so current vendor positions may be stale.
Several vendor newsroom URLs recorded here (Diebold Nixdorf, NCR Atleos, BPC, Worldline) were inferred as standard newsroom paths and were not fetched in this pass.
Historical sponsor and speaker rosters for ME events (INFINTECH, IT SPOT, Spark.me, SCMN Montenegro Financial Markets) are not available on the live sites; only the current edition is published.
Sponsor tiers on ME event sites are largely logo walls; several sponsor names could not be extracted from text alone.
The key local trade portal (bankar.me) is bot-defended and social event pages (LinkedIn/Facebook) are login-walled, so two of the richest sponsor/partnership channels are not plain-HTTP collectable.

No ME-run industry award with a published shortlist was found, so the 'awards' half of this cell is currently served only by foreign awards (The Banker, Global Finance) whose citations rarely name the technology vendor.

Montenegrin/Serbian-language coverage of REGIONAL events (how ME banks appear at Money Motion, BANCEE, Kopaonik-type forums) was not established — regional event sites publish in English/Croatian only.
Vendor-hosted private events (bank roadshows, closed user-group meetings, Visa/Mastercard client days in ME) leave almost no public trace and were not captured.
Vijesti (vijesti.me) — the cell's most prominent named outlet — has no confirmed section URL or article evidence from this run.
Standard (standard.co.me) and other second-tier ME dailies/portals were referenced only indirectly (via traffic-analytics pages) and never inspected.

Social and video channels of these outlets (Facebook pages for Bankar.me and Portal Analitika, X/@PortalAnalitika, LinkedIn pages for CKB and CBCG) were observed in indexes but not assessed as collection channels.
No archival/back-catalogue strategy exists for these outlets; most were assessed only on current front pages and recent articles.
The cell mandates sr and en; sr coverage was thorough, but no en-language Montenegrin business outlet (e.g. English editions or expat/business-English portals) was identified.
Several ME portals publish syndicated bank PR indistinguishable from editorial (the same 'Partnerstvo koje pokreće uspjeh' item ran on both CdM and sjevercg.me).
Bosnian (Sarajevo / Banja Luka) vendor leg of the regional spillover is unmapped: no BiH integrator was evidenced as serving Montenegro.
No Croatian-language query set was executed against Croatian integrator and fintech sites despite Zagreb being a primary delivery hub for Montenegro.

No procurement/tender source was captured for Montenegrin banks or state financial institutions; state-owned or state-influenced entities (Razvojna banka Crne Gore, Centralna banka Crne Gore, Pošta Crne Gore) publish tenders naming IT scopes and winning regional bidders.

Vendor-to-bank attribution exists for only a few of Montenegro's ~11 banks (NLB Banka Podgorica, Adriatic Bank, partially CKB). Hipotekarna, Erste ME, Lovcen, Prva, Universal Capital, Ziraat, Addiko ME, Zapad banka remain unattributed.
Regional bank groups' annual reports and IR decks (NLB, OTP, Intesa, Erste, Addiko, Ziraat) were not mined; these disclose digitalisation programmes and capex rolled down to ME subsidiaries.
LinkedIn (both ME bank company pages/job posts and vendor posts tagging ME clients) is unreadable under current tooling and terms.
Second-instance judicial review of procurement appeals (Upravni sud Crne Gore) and the e-procurement award record (CEJN/ESJN portal) were not reached.
Platform-name evidence inside job ads was never actually observed — only the containers were found.

Only CKB, NLB, Prva banka, Erste and Ziraat surfaced; the full licensed-bank list (incl. Hipotekarna, Universal Capital Bank, Adriatic Bank, Lovćen banka, Zapad banka, Addiko) plus payment institutions and the card processor layer were not individually swept for job ads or LinkedIn presence.
No developer/tech-stack fingerprinting source (GitHub orgs, ME bank mobile-app SDK teardowns, TLS/HTTP header or app-store metadata fingerprints) was established.

Mid-tier and local advisory firms on the ICAM register (BDO, Crowe MNE, HLB Mont Audit, TPA, Baker-Tilly-equivalents, Auditor DOO, Racio-Mont) have not been profiled for banking-sector clients or publications.
EBRD (country strategy, Transition Report, project summary documents, technical-assistance procurement) is unscouted.
Credit-rating agency layer (Moody's, S&P, Fitch, plus regional agencies) for Montenegrin banks and their parent groups is only inferred.
The World Bank digital-payments loan is identified only via a press release; project ID, procurement plan and contract awards (STEP) are not yet located.

Local-language coverage used sr terms for audit/reporting (revizija, revizorski izvještaj, finansijski iskazi, bankarski sektor) but not for adviser-side marketing vocabulary (digitalna transformacija banaka, konsultantske usluge, due diligence, savjetodavne usluge) or Montenegrin-specific orthography variants.
Individual bank annual reports hosted on bank websites (rather than cbcg.me) were not enumerated; several carry richer notes on software capex and outsourcing.
No enumerated list yet of Montenegrin/regional IT and payment vendors serving ME banks, nor their current and historical domains — the prerequisite input for archive enumeration.
Merged/liquidated Montenegrin banks (the richest archive targets) were not enumerated; only the current CBCG register page was located.
ujn.gov.me was identified but its award/contract notice listings were not opened, so no ME state IT/payment contract award has actually been read in this pass.

The cell explicitly names the digital-agenda administration, but the current body responsible for state IT operations (successor to MJUDDM functions, e.g. a Uprava/Direktorat for digitalisation and information security) was not located, so its project and contractor pages are uncovered.
EU/UNDP/World Bank funded digital projects in ME publish their own tender awards, a channel touched only via one UNDP press release.

Local-language coverage was met for gazette, strategy and payment terms, but no sr searches were run for archive-specific vocabulary ('arhivirana stranica', 'web arhiva', 'obavezni primjerak', 'Državni arhiv Crne Gore') or for vendor-reference vocabulary ('lista referenci', 'uspješni projekti', 'studija slučaja').

Newsroom/announcement paths remain unmapped for Zapad banka, Universal Capital Bank, Lovćen banka and Ziraat Bank Montenegro. NLB's and CKB's news listing (as opposed to detail) pages are also not yet pinned down.

Only the CKB 2024 audited statements PDF was located concretely. The equivalent annual reports and audited financial statements for the other nine banks were not individually enumerated in this pass, and no multi-year historical series was assembled for any bank.

App-store package-id fingerprinting proved to be the single highest-yield vendor-attribution method in this cell, but it was applied opportunistically to only five banks (Prva, Ziraat, NLB, Hipotekarna, Lovćen). CKB, Erste ME, Adriatic, Zapad and Universal Capital were not fingerprinted.

Product terms-and-conditions PDFs ('opšti uslovi poslovanja', 'opšti uslovi za e-banking', card and payment-services terms) were sampled for only two banks (Ziraat, CKB). These documents must name the operator of a service and are therefore a structurally reliable vendor-reveal artifact that this pass barely touched.

A LinkedIn profile for a Bankart d.o.o. employee surfaced in a query about ME banks' new system implementation, hinting that the Slovenian card-processing house Bankart may serve Montenegrin banks. This was not corroborated by any bank-side or Bankart-side source in this pass.

The national instant-payments rollout coordinated by CBCG (with Bank of Italy, ECB and World Bank support) involved these banks and is the largest recent ME payments programme, but no bank-side communication about its technical implementation was located.

Two of the highest-signal channels for the smaller banks (LinkedIn and Meta feeds) are login-gated and ToS-restricted against automated collection, yet they are where those banks actually announce launches.
Unknown whether OTP (Budapest) and Erste Group Procurement (Vienna) run sourcing for their Montenegrin subsidiaries centrally, and whether Ariba/EGP events are ever visible externally.
Print and online classified/oglasi channels (Pobjeda, Vijesti, Dan) where Montenegrin banks place statutory and commercial notices were not searched in this run.
Bank social-media channels were only incidentally covered, yet a CKB 'javni poziv' was found on Facebook rather than the website.
etenderi.me — the most promising ME-native aggregator with competitor-win analytics and an OCR'd archive of State Commission decisions — could not be inspected.

Procurement-appeal jurisprudence (Komisija za kontrolu postupka javnih nabavki decisions) was identified only indirectly via etenderi.me's archive; the primary body's own decision database was not located.
Other IFI/donor procurement routes touching Montenegrin banks (IFC, World Bank, EIB, EU IPA) were not searched; only EBRD/ECEPP was covered.

Hungarian and German were used for the OTP and Erste parents, but no Turkish-language check was made for Ziraat Bank Montenegro's parent sourcing, and no Slovenian-language check of NLB's local supplier terms beyond generic ones.
No mapped machine interface to CeJN (no confirmed JSON endpoint, no known id range, no CPV filter syntax).

Not all state-owned buyers relevant to cash/payments were individually verified: notably Investiciono-razvojni fond (IRF), Fond PIO, Fond za zdravstveno osiguranje, Aerodromi Crne Gore, Luka Bar, Crnogorski Telekom (partly state-linked), Uprava za katastar, and the Ministarstvo javne uprave (digital society) as an IT buyer.

State IT work placed via intergovernmental 'sporazumi' and via direktni sporazum below thresholds never appears as a competitive award, so CeJN-only tracking understates and biases the competitor picture.

No CPV code list or controlled keyword set has yet been fixed for the ME cell; keyword recall in a Montenegrin corpus is fragile (bankomat/bankomati, POS terminal/POS terminali/PoS, kartic-/kartica/kartice/kartično poslovanje, platni promet, instant placanja, gotovinsko poslovanje, brojaci novca, personalizacija kartica, HSM, core banking, softverske licence).
Historical depth of CeJN is unknown — it replaced an earlier portal (portal.ujn.gov.me era). Pre-2020 award history may not be retrievable from CeJN at all.
Many CeJN award documents are scanned images (visible in the garbled OCR of mirrored PDFs such as 'oeev.,eSrENJE o rsHoDU PosruPKA'), so supplier names and values are not reliably text-extractable.
Council of Europe Development Bank (CEB), Green for Growth Fund / EFSE and other EU-blended financial-sector funds active in the Western Balkans were not searched in this pass.
TED Search API and World Bank STEP/Finances One datasets were identified but neither query syntax nor a working ME+finance CPV filter has been validated.
Montenegro's national IPA contract register (CFCU / indirect-management contract lists under the Ministry of Finance) was not located as a discrete published dataset.
For the flagship WB SEPA/TIPS-clone project, the beneficiary and technical solution (Banca d'Italia TIPS clone) are known but no procurement package or awarded implementer has yet been identified.

Only four of the ~11 ME banks' acquiring/POS/e-commerce pages were identified (CKB, Hipotekarna, Erste ME, Addiko). NLB Banka CG, Universal Capital Bank, Prva banka, Lovćen banka, Adriatic Bank, Ziraat, Zapad banka and others are uncovered.
No procurement/tender source was covered for payments contracts (bank and state-owned enterprise POS/gateway tenders, CBCG procurement).
Company-registry and ownership verification not covered for payments entities (e.g. Payten d.o.o. Montenegro, local PSPs).
No technical-fingerprint sweep of ME merchant checkouts was performed to infer which gateway each large ME e-merchant uses.

Non-card payments-native players in ME are thinly covered: money-transfer payment institutions (e.g. Montenegro Transfers, Moneta MNE / MoneyGram agency), Pošta Crne Gore financial services, and telco-adjacent wallets.
Searching was done in Montenegrin/Serbian Latin only; Cyrillic-script and Albanian-language (Ulcinj/Tuzi minority-business) variants were not tried.

The eleven licensed Montenegrin banks were not individually profiled as scheme/infrastructure participants. Their own newsrooms, general terms & conditions for cards and payment services, and annual reports frequently name the card processor, switch, gateway and 3-D Secure provider.

No source yet ties a named technology supplier to CBCG's RTGS/DNS platform (in operation over 20 years) or to the bank-side connectivity layer for TIPS Clone. The settlement platform provider is known (Banca d'Italia), but the surrounding stack is unattributed.
SWIFT-side sources (national member/user group, BIC directory, service bureaux serving ME) were not covered in this pass.
The Central Depository Agency (CDA/CDA Montenegro) — the national CSD identified in the World Bank FSAP note — was not scouted, nor were securities settlement links to the payment system.

CBCG press releases use id-parameterised URLs and the listing pagination depth was not explored; historical announcements (pre-2024 SEPA/TIPS milestones, earlier RTGS upgrades) are not yet inventoried.

Local-language coverage was strong for CBCG, SEPA and instant payments, but thin for card-scheme certification vocabulary — 'kartična šema', 'sertifikacija', 'procesing centar' returned mostly consumer bank product pages rather than industry sources.

Card processors / payment processors and ATM-network operators have no dedicated ME register; they must be inferred from payment-system operator entries, payment-institution service lines, and CRPS NACE codes.
Every register found is an HTML page or a PDF; no confirmed bulk download, API or CSV extract for CRPS company data or for the CBCG licence registers.
Two parallel company-register front-ends were observed (pretraga.crps.me under CRPS, and irms.tax.gov.me under the Revenue and Customs Administration). Which is canonical going forward is unresolved.
SCMN (capital market) and ANO (insurance) licence registers were confirmed to exist but not located at URL level.

No mapping was built from KD 2010 / NACE Rev.2 activity codes to the payments-and-banking-technology segments of interest, so CRPS and MONSTAT activity-based enumeration cannot yet be executed precisely.
CBCG serves the same content under at least four locale prefixes (/me/, /eng/, /r/, /c/) and at least one register exists under both a correct and a misspelled slug ('insitucije').
It is unclear how much of the CRPS beneficial-ownership register is publicly readable versus gated behind a qualified digital certificate.

Local-language (sr/Montenegrin) coverage was strong and drove nearly every discovery; English-language searching added almost nothing new beyond the exchange and CBCG mirror pages, and no EU-level register (EBA/ECB) covers Montenegro since it is not an EU member state.
AmCham member-list, publications and committee URLs were inferred from the homepage navigation rather than fetched; the exact paths are unconfirmed.
Non-US/non-German foreign chambers were not covered: no search was run for Italian, French, Turkish, Chinese or UK business associations in Montenegro, and no Nordic/EU business council.

Insurance, leasing, microcredit and payment-institution trade bodies (e.g. any Udruženje osiguravača / leasing association) were not separately scouted; they were only reached indirectly through the PKCG combined finance board.

Association newsletters as a channel (email bulletins, LinkedIn pages) were only partially mapped; UBCG, PKCG, AmCham and ICT Cortex LinkedIn feeds often carry event and partnership announcements earlier than the websites.
PDF serial archives (Bankar magazine, Glasnik PKCG, MFIC White Books) were identified but their full issue enumeration and date ranges were not established.
